published_contract.experiment: distance-three repetition-code X-memory over three stabilizer rounds
published_contract.physical_channel: Eq. (9) coherent over-rotation at theta=0.05 at the beginning of each round
published_contract.decoder_family: PyMatching initialized from a Pauli-twirled detector error model

indispensable_unpublished_inputs: the exact ordered noiseless circuit and ancilla schedule emitted by the Plaquette Code object
the precise error-location selectors and before/after-gate composition convention used for the run
the compiled detector error model and resulting PyMatching graph and edge weights
the sampler-specific compilation and logical-observable/frame conventions

non_uniqueness_test.statement: The printed distance, round count, channel, decoder family, and shot counts admit multiple circuit schedules, error placements, detector models, and frame conventions with different logical-failure probabilities; they do not uniquely define the reported 38.7% calculation.

availability_boundary.statement: The paper states that supporting data are available only from the authors on request and that Plaquette is a commercial product; neither supplies a frozen independently auditable numerical input deck in the publication.

clean_room_attempt.outcome: The independently declared proxy reproduces the published channel invariants and qualitative ordering but not the paper-exact coherent logical-error value.

conclusion: The public equations support an independent proxy calculation, but a paper-exact Fig. 5(a) calculation is objectively blocked by publication-level underspecification rather than by missing reproduction code or local compute.
